panels.rationale: This is a real patient H&E histology image of bone tissue from a case of Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome, showing characteristic thickened remodeled cortical bone with enlarged Haversian canals consistent with histologic osteopoikilosis (the osseous manifestation of the disease), with no exclusion criteria applicable.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the patient's lower extremities showing the medial left lower extremity with reticular skin lesions (elastoma), a manifestation of Buschke-Ollendorff Syndrome as confirmed by biopsy and described in the case report. B: Close-up clinical photograph of the left knee region showing reticular skin lesions consistent with elastoma (connective tissue nevus) in Buschke-Ollendorff Syndrome. C: Close-up clinical photograph of the left ankle/foot showing reticular skin lesions consistent with elastoma (connective tissue nevus) in Buschke-Ollendorff Syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Aydın Şimşek et al. Buschke-Ollendorff Syndrome: A Rare Cause of Unilateral Genu Valgum.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.38074. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Reticular skin lesions on the medial surface of the left lower extremity.
in_text_mentions: In further physical examination, the patient had flexion contracture in the left knee, and skin lesions were observed with a reticular pattern over the medial part of the left lower extremity (Figure 2). It was learned that these lesions had developed since birth and were permanent. The patient was referred to the dermatology department, and the pathology result of the skin biopsy supported the diagnosis of elastoma.
